exposure: late gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) diagnosis (>34 weeks)
cohort: The study assessed obstetrical and neonatal outcomes of 238 women who had normal glucose screening results between 24-28 weeks but underwent late repeat oral glucose tolerance tests (>34 weeks) due to a suspected LGA fetus or polyhydramnios.
finding: Late third-trimester GDM diagnosis in women with previously normal glucose screening, particularly those with morbid obesity or suspected fetal growth issues, is associated with a higher risk of adverse perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: A higher risk for Cesarean section (CS) due to macrosomia was demonstrated in women with late GDM compared to those with mid-trimester GDM.
